descriptionChirho: An adverb of frequency meaning 'two times,' used in contexts of repeated action or comparison. Spanish 'dos veces,' Hindi 'do bar,' Arabic 'marratayni,' Korean 'du beon,' Swahili 'mara mbili.' Examples include the Pharisee fasting twice a week (Luke 18:12), Peter denying before the cock crows twice (Mark 14:30, 72), Jude 12 'twice dead,' and Philippians 4:16 sending aid twice. All six occurrences share this straightforward multiplicative-adverbial meaning.

A numeral expression meaning 'two myriads' or 'twenty thousand' used in the compound dismyriades myriados ('two hundred million') in Rev 9:16 to describe the vast army of horsemen. Spanish 'dos miriadas,' Hindi 'bis karod,' Arabic 'ribwatu,' Korean 'iman,' Swahili 'mia mbili milioni.' This is functionally a distinct lexical sense from the adverb 'twice,' serving as a cardinal numeral multiplier rather than a frequency adverb, as shown by the divergent translation signatures across all target languages.
